- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the latter half of the 30-day window, particularly after a spike in the middle.
- Model shows strong lag in reacting to recent price increases — forecasts lag behind true price movements by 5–10 days.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects with a downward bias.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overestimates when prices are low, underestimates when prices are high, but fails to capture the true momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases following a low point, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Model overestimates the rate of decline after a spike, then underestimates the subsequent recovery.
- Model fails to capture the true volatility clustering — underestimates sharp moves and overestimates smooth transitions.
- Model is overly conservative in the first 5–7 days, then becomes more aggressive in the final 10–15 days.
- Model does not adjust for the “recovery bias” — tends to assume prices will return to prior levels without accounting for sustained momentum.
